# Metaprogramming

Edva compile-time execution uses `#!`. Compile-time values are erased: a value
of `Type` cannot exist at runtime. There are no runtime type descriptors or
reflection tables.

## Evaluate a constant

Prefix `#!` evaluates a supported pure expression during compilation:

```dva
answer = #! 2 * 3 + 1
print_int $ answer
```

Use `#size(Type)` to obtain the byte size of a type at compile time.

## Generic functions

A `#! T: Type` parameter is a compile-time type parameter. It is inferred at
the call site and does not become a runtime parameter.

```dva
identity: #! T: Type, T => T
identity = value => value

print_int $ identity(42)
```

Compile-time value parameters use the same form with an ordinary type, such as
`#! N: Int`. Type generators return a type shape and are named with `#type`.

```dva
Pair: #! T: Type => (first: T, count: Int)
#type IntPair Pair(Int)
```

Use type predicates and compile-time choices to specialize code by shape. Keep
compile-time work pure and statically resolvable; the compiler reports an error
when a compile-time value would escape to runtime. See the
[Types reference](../reference/types/index.qmd) for type representations,
reflection, and supported compile-time forms.
